precepts.text: Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. There is no healing without confession. You can't cherry-pick what you want out of the Bible and expect to be received of God.
precepts.point: The first step of changing is to acknowledge that we have issues.

note.label: Pay The Price: Pleasure Now Regret Later

precepts.why:
The Pharisees asked, “Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?” Why is Christ sitting and communicating with ungodly people? To bring them to repentance. That was the whole purpose: “I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” So if you think you're right, then he's not here for you. The first step of changing is to acknowledge that we have issues.

James shows that first step: “Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed.” You have to confess your faults so that we can pray for you and you can be healed. There is no healing without confession.

You can't cherry-pick what you want out of the Bible and expect to be received of God and Christ. Christ said, I came for the sick, those that need healing. But the sick have to own that they are sick. Many people are right in their own eyes; we don't want to see ourselves in a negative light and we act like the parts of us that aren't right will be all right with God. We will fall short of the kingdom if we keep that mindset of not changing.

So confession is where the physician's work begins. The one who acknowledges his faults can be prayed for and healed; the one who hides them, looking the part with fringes and a beard, stays sick.

precepts.text: Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. We should be comfortable confessing our faults, because no temptation has taken you but such as is common to man. You confess to a brother and he says, brother, I was dealing with the same spirit, and you feel a lot better. Everybody deals with a level of bitterness, of lust, of lack of faith. That is not getting on the public announcement; it is finding a godly man and saying, I have this going on, I need help. They are going to help you.
precepts.point: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: when you try to cover that bitterness, the roots keep growing; you are just hauling in more soil to dump on top of the stump. But whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy: that is what we all want.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Confessing is not only to the Lord. James says: “Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.”

We should be comfortable confessing our faults, because, as 1 Corinthians 10:13 says, no temptation has taken you but such as is common to man. You confess your fault, and a brother might say, brother, I was dealing with the same spirit. Woo, man, I feel a lot better. All of this is common. We all have levels of bitterness; some have a higher degree than others, but everybody deals with a level of bitterness, a level of lust, a level of lack of faith.

That doesn't mean getting on the public announcement. It means you see a godly man and say, hey Cap, hey D, I have this going on, I need help with it. They are going to help you. They are not going to say, brother, you got the devil on you, get away from me. It is Satan telling us otherwise.

That is whoso confesseth and forsaketh: confessing to the Lord, confessing one to another, and being healed, instead of covering the sin and letting the root grow.

precepts.text: Let your communication be yea, yea; nay, nay: whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil. Lying to your brothers is evil, and evil is condemned by the Lord, who rewards every man according to his deeds.
precepts.point: If the Lord exposes you through people volunteering your business unasked, he wants you to get right before you do it to the wrong person and the brothers find out at your funeral. You can hate the messenger or recognize the mercy, apologize, make amends, and walk in the spirit.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

precepts.why:
“let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation.” When you say yes, I am going to do it, do it. When you say no, you can’t, then don’t. But never say yes, get paid to do the job, and then not do it. Christ put it this way: “But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.”

You are evil when you lie to your brothers. Anything other than yea and nay is evil, and if you are evil you are going to be condemned: not by us, but by the Lord. Condemn means to declare reprehensible, wrong or evil, usually after weighing evidence. The Lord is going to review your case like a court docket: the state versus so-and-so, how do you plead, not guilty, bring the witness. He didn’t know they had the witnesses.

The eyes of the Lord are in every place, beholding the evil and the good, and he rewards every man according to his deeds. Curse not the king in your chamber, lest a bird carry the news. You do evil in a different state with somebody we never met, and another brother goes to that state for a job and meets the same person. After a joyful Sabbath together, two brothers got in the car, one pocket-dialed the captain, and he heard them talking trash about all the ranking men. When questioned, the first thing was a lie.

When people bring up your evil without anybody asking one question, the Lord is exposing you because he wants you to get right. He could have let you do it to the wrong person, and we find out at your funeral: he stole a hundred grand and a dude put two in his back. You can sit home and hate the messenger, or recognize the mistake, apologize, make amends and walk in the spirit so blessing comes your way. The choice is yours.

precepts.text: Lie not one to another. We must be men of honour so the world says surely this is a wise and understanding people. You cannot be in the Bible and doing evil at the same time; the word has to be far from your head for you to do it.
precepts.point: If the Lord exposes you through people volunteering your business unasked, he wants you to get right before you do it to the wrong person and the brothers find out at your funeral. You can hate the messenger or recognize the mercy, apologize, make amends, and walk in the spirit.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

precepts.why:
“Lie not one to another, seeing that ye have put off the old man with his deeds.” It is forbidden for us to lie one to another. We must be men of character, men of honour, because the world must look at us and say, surely this is a wise and understanding people. If you are lying, how is the world going to say that? They will say this is an evil-ass negro, and the truth gets evil spoken of, because the whole time you were doing it you had fringes on your clothes.

At no time did you look down at your fringes and say, damn, I can’t behave this way, I can’t do this to my brother, not even to people in the world. Why? Because you are not in the Bible. There is no way you are in the Bible and doing evil at the same time; it is an oxymoron. You just finished reading thou shalt not steal, I love that scripture, let me get my gun? It doesn’t go that way. The word has to be nowhere near your head for you to go do evil. That is why you stay in this Bible and give attendance to reading, continuously, so the word is in you.

A bishop “must have a good report of them which are without; lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.” People in the world will lie on us, but they should never be able to back it up. In business in the world you must be twice as honourable, and you will get more jobs, because nobody likes a thief. Penny wise, pound foolish: make an extra penny now and lose the whole pound. Lie and steal, and you end up ducking people, circling the block, getting beaten over twenty dollars, and still owing the money. The devil convinced you it was okay to lie, then removed himself. Put off the old man and his deeds, and lie not one to another.

precepts.text: Above all things, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath; lest ye fall into condemnation.
precepts.point: Swearing on the Bible in the court system is another matter: be subject unto the higher powers, for the powers that be are ordained of God, and you also have the option to affirm; either way, tell the truth.

note.label: Numbers 30: The Law of Vows

precepts.why:
James says the same as Christ, and puts it first: “But above all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath: but let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation.”

A man who vows a vow and does not perform it falls into condemnation, for the Lord will surely require it. So above all things, swear not; let your yea be yea and your nay, nay. That is why we say the Lord’s will rather than binding our souls with an oath.

precepts.text: The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much; that is why they told Samuel, do not stop praying for us.
precepts.point: When the lords of the Philistines heard Israel was gathered at Mizpeh, they came up against Israel again, and Israel was afraid. But this time, instead of running for the ark, the children of Israel charged Samuel, Cease not to cry unto the Lord our God for us, that he will save us out of the hand of the Philistines. They knew the prayer of a righteous man reaches the ears of the Most High.

note.label: 1 Samuel 7: Put Away the Strange Gods, and the Lord Thundered

precepts.why:
“The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.” That is why Israel told Samuel, do not stop praying for us: “Cease not to cry unto the Lord our God for us, that he will save us out of the hand of the Philistines.”

Israel had gathered to Mizpeh, drawn water and poured it out before the Lord, fasted, and confessed, “We have sinned against the Lord.” That is James's order too: “Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed.”

When the lords of the Philistines came up again and Israel was afraid, this time they did not run for the ark. They went to the righteous man, because they knew the prayer of a righteous man reaches the ears of the Most High.

precepts.text: Confess your faults one to another and pray one for another, for the effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much, and it was Job's righteous prayer that spared his friends.
precepts.point: Then all his brethren, sisters, and former acquaintances came and ate bread with him, bemoaned him, and comforted him over all the evil the Most High had brought upon him, and every man gave him a piece of money and an earring of gold. After his captivity was turned his friends returned as well.

note.label: Job 42: The Lord Turned the Captivity of Job

precepts.why:
“And the Lord turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends”. James shows why that prayer worked: “Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.”

It was not the prayer alone that availed, but the prayer of a righteous man. It was Job's righteous prayer that spared his friends, and the Most High deals with those that are dealing in righteousness. When Job prayed for them, the Lord turned his captivity and gave him twice as much as he had before, and after his captivity was turned his brethren, his sisters and his former acquaintances returned as well.

precepts.text: Is any sick among you? let him call for the elders of the church to pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord.
precepts.point: In the last days the pattern is to call the elders of the church to pray over the sick and anoint with oil, for prophecies, tongues, and such knowledge would cease once the name of Christ was established.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
The pattern for the last days: “Is any sick among you? let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord”.

Not the shadow of an apostle, not a healing line. The sick call for the elders of the church, who pray over him and anoint him with oil in the name of the Lord.

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

points: From Trauma Letters, letter six, a son writing to his father: your absence affected my emotional intelligence. No one taught me how to process emotion. Men are often frowned upon in society for expressing how they feel. We are told to suppress, to be strong, to not break down. So I buried sadness, I converted fear into anger, I wore a mask so convincing even I forgot what was underneath. In order to be relieved of this internal pain we must learn to process and channel it through God's word, but I never learned this type of emotional stability; in your absence I learned to just not deal with it, not knowing the emotional and spiritual toll it was taking on me.

Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. Men do not like doing that. Brothers will name you as their counselor of a thousand and never actually call you to counsel about anything they are dealing with. They do not want to say they do not have a counselor, but they do not have one.
We do not know how to process what happened to us in our past, so we keep it bottled up, and we do not take it out on our boss or the congregation. We take it out on our spouse.
